newsitem.title: CANADA: Chile and Argentina close to mining protocol.
newsitem.headline: Chile and Argentina close to mining protocol.

text.p: Chile and Argentina are close to finalizing protocols that will make cross-border mineral exploration easier for two Canadian companies, Barrick Gold Corp and Cambior Inc, Chile's minister of mining said in Toronto on Tuesday.
The protocols should be signed in the beginning of December, Benjamin Teplizky said at a Chile-Canada trade conference.
"Barrick and Cambior will be the first ones to benefit," he said, speaking in Spanish. "It will be a chance perhaps unique in the world."
The two countries are working on a treaty to allow the free flow of mining goods and equipment across their borders, but the treaty has been tied up in government processes.
The protocols will allow the two Canadian companies cross-border access without having to wait for the treaty. The companies will be able to use their Chilean infrastructure to explore in Argentina.
"This is a major step forward for the whole industry," Barrick chairman Peter Munk said at the conference.
The protocol will speed up exploration in Barrick's Lama prospect in Argentina, on the other side of the border from Barrick's Pascua project in Chile, said John Lill, president of Barrick in Chile.
The protocol is also expected to help Cambior's Pachn copper project.
